answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a hollow as the anchor of the cost.
